tools.name: search_guidelines
tools.description:
Look a rule up in the UMR guidelines (umr4nlp/umr-guidelines, guidelines.md).

keywords: terms to look for, e.g. "aspect", "modal strength", "have-rel-role-92", ":quant",
"reentrancy". Passages with more of the keywords come first, then those whose heading has
them, then those that mention them most.
max_results: how many passages to return (at most 10).

Returns {"sections": [{"heading": the passage's place in the guidelines ("Part 3. ... > Part
3-3-1. Aspect"), "text": the passage (a section, or a part of a long one)}], "found": how
many passages matched}.

tools.name: propbank_lookup
tools.description:
Look up a lemma and every alternate of it in PropBank (at most 20 per call).

language is "en" or "zh". Returns Markdown: per lemma, every roleset with its roles and all
its examples (the sentence, then each argument; traces such as *T*-1 are PropBank's own),
or "not in PropBank". Lemmas over the limit are not looked up: the last line names them
(call again with them). There is no PropBank for another language (Uzbek): nothing.

tools.name: search_annotations
tools.description:
Find how a case is annotated: gold UMR annotations of whole sentences.

language: "zh" (Chinese) or "en" (English).
keywords: words or pieces to look for, matched anywhere in a sentence or its annotation:
words of the text (e.g. "发生", "wanted to"), concepts ("have-org-role-91", "identity-91"),
roles (":ARG1-of", ":manner"), attribute values (":aspect state"). Sentences with more of the
keywords come first.
max_results: how many gold sentences to return (at most 10).

Returns {"gold": [{"doc", "sentence_number", "sentence", "annotation"}], where annotation is
the sentence's whole annotation (words, sentence-level graph, alignment, document-level
annotation); "found": how many gold sentences matched in all}.

messages.content:
## Input

Language: zh
Document: zh-0028, sentence 3 of 12

The previous sentences (at most five; number, tab, words):

1	16 : 9 的 屏幕 比例 、 21.5 英寸 宽屏 ， 它 的 最佳 分辨率 为 1920 × 1080 ，

2	而且 它 还 配备 了 D-Sub （ VGA ） ， HDMI 两 种 接口 ，

Their graphs:

The sentence reads as a list of three specs for one display: "16:9 screen ratio, 21.5-inch widescreen, its best resolution is 1920×1080." I joined the three parts with an `and` and annotated "为" as `identity-91`. I found no gold examples with 分辨率, 英寸 or 屏幕, so these choices are mine and not copied from the data:

- **16:9:** I wrote the ratio as a `string-entity` holding "16:9" and linked it with `:quant`.
- **1920 × 1080:** I wrote it as `product-of` with the two numbers.
- **21.5 英寸:** this is a `distance-quantity` with 英寸 as its unit.
- **最佳:** I kept it as one modifier word, not split into 佳 plus a degree marker.
- **它:** this is a `thing` (3rd person, singular) and is the possessor of the resolution.

    # ::snt 1
    # sentence level graph:
    (s1a / and
        :op1 (s1x / 比例
            :mod (s1x2 / 屏幕)
            :quant (s1r / string-entity
                :value "16:9"))
        :op2 (s1x3 / 宽屏
            :mod (s1d / distance-quantity
                :quant 21.5
                :unit (s1x4 / 英寸)))
        :op3 (s1i / identity-91
            :ARG1 (s1x5 / 分辨率
                :mod (s1x6 / 最佳)
                :possessor (s1t / thing
                    :refer-person 3rd
                    :refer-number singular))
            :ARG2 (s1p / product-of
                :op1 1920
                :op2 1080)
            :aspect state))

I annotated sentence 2 as follows:

- **Main predicate:** 配备 is PropBank `配备-01`. Its ARG0 is the agent, ARG1 the thing equipped and ARG2 the place it is fitted to. In 它配备了…接口, 它 is the device the ports are on, so I made it `:ARG2`, as in PropBank's examples. There is no agent. 它 is a 3rd-person singular `thing`.
- **Aspect:** 了 marks a completed event, so the aspect is `performance`.
- **而且 and 还:** both are `:mod` nodes. The gold examples of 而且 I found were partial conversions using `progression`, which isn't a standard concept, so I didn't follow them.
- **The ports:** 接口 has `:quant 2`. 种 is a classifier, so it gets no node. The search found no gold example with 接口 to copy.
- **The listed ports:** I put the two port types under `:mod` as an `and` of two named `product`s. "VGA" in brackets is an alternative name for D-Sub, so I attached it to D-Sub as another `:mod` product. Both are judgement calls. The list names every port, so an identity-style reading would also be defensible, and VGA could have been treated as a second name.

# ::snt 2
# sentence level graph:
(s2x / 配备-01
    :ARG2 (s2t / thing
        :refer-person 3rd
        :refer-number singular)
    :ARG1 (s2j / 接口
        :quant 2
        :mod (s2a / and
            :op1 (s2p / product
                :name (s2n / name :op1 "D-Sub")
                :mod (s2p2 / product
                    :name (s2n2 / name :op1 "VGA")))
            :op2 (s2p3 / product
                :name (s2n3 / name :op1 "HDMI"))))
    :mod (s2e / 而且)
    :mod (s2h / 还)
    :aspect performance)

This sentence:

3	能够 在 拨接 电脑 设备 之 余 ， 还 能够 方便 用户 进行 PS3 、 Xbox360 、 蓝光机 等等 设备 的 连接 。

Its graph:

# ::snt 3
# sentence level graph:
(s3f / 方便-01
    :ARG0 (s3t / thing
        :refer-person 3rd
        :refer-number singular)
    :ARG1 (s3u / 用户)
    :ARG2 (s3l / 连接-01
        :ARG0 s3u
        :ARG1 (s3s / 设备
            :example (s3a / and
                :op1 (s3p / product
                    :name (s3n / name :op1 "PS3"))
                :op2 (s3p2 / product
                    :name (s3n2 / name :op1 "Xbox360"))
                :op3 (s3b / 蓝光机)
                :op4 (s3e / et-cetera)))
        :aspect state)
    :temporal (s3b2 / 拨接-01
        :ARG0 s3t
        :ARG1 (s3s2 / 设备
            :mod (s3d / 电脑))
        :aspect state
        :modal-strength neutral-affirmative)
    :mod (s3h / 还)
    :aspect state
    :modal-strength neutral-affirmative)

content.text:
# document level relations:
(d / document
    :temporal ((document-creation-time :overlap s3f)
               (s3f :overlap s3b2)
               (s3f :overlap s3l))
    :modal ((root :modal author)
            (author :neutral-affirmative s3f)
            (author :neutral-affirmative s3b2)
            (author :neutral-affirmative s3l))
    :coref ((s2t :same-entity s3t)))

I did not use the search or PropBank tools for this sentence. These relations follow the abridged guidelines and my own reading, and are not checked against gold examples.

- **Temporal:** The sentence describes what the display can generally do, so I treated 方便 (s3f) as a present state that overlaps the document creation time. Connecting computer devices (拨接, s3b2) is attached to s3f as its time, so I put it under s3f with `:overlap`. The users' connecting (连接, s3l) is also under s3f with `:overlap`, as a state.
- **Modal:** All three events come after 能够 ("can"), so each gets `neutral-affirmative` from the author. For 连接, the guidelines' rule for complements would instead put it under 方便 with `unspecified`. I didn't take that option because 方便 is not really a modal predicate, but it is a judgement call.
- **Coreference:** 它 here (s3t) is the same display as 它 in sentence 2 (s2t), so I linked it to that closest earlier mention.
